summary.text: A 57-year-old man without known comorbidities or risk factors for venous thromboembolism came to the emergency room with mild dyspnea and persistent right lower limb edema that began about a month earlier, with 3 days of fever and shivering. On examination he was afebrile, in good general health and dyspneic in room air, with normal auscultation, right leg edema, white blood count 12,150 without left shift, hematocrit 41%, and normal CK-MB, electrolytes, urea and creatinine.

Echocardiogram, electrocardiogram and chest X-ray were unremarkable. Doppler ultrasonography showed acute thrombosis of the right popliteal and soleus veins. Chest CTA showed no pneumonia but bilateral pulmonary artery thrombus with right pulmonary infarction, and a rapid COVID-19 test was IgG positive and IgM negative. D-dimer and C-reactive protein were not available. The diagnostic hypothesis was extensive acute pulmonary embolism complicating oligosymptomatic COVID-19.

He received intravenous Alteplase (10 mg then 90 mg over 2 hours) without hemodynamic instability or fibrinolytic complications. Dyspnea improved, and a repeat chest CTA 9 hours after the first showed good restoration of flow and resolution of much of the thrombus. Forty-eight hours after admission he began acetylsalicylic acid 100 mg/day and clopidogrel 75 mg/day.

He was discharged after 6 days in hospital because of re-infection risk and bed needs. Outpatient follow-up was not possible because clinics were suspended, so he was instructed to maintain dual antiaggregation and return to the emergency room for warning signs or clinical deterioration.
